bib.title: LLM-based Agents for Automated Bug Fixing: How Far Are We?
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v2, 19 Oct 2025; template text reads 'Conference acronym XX, June 03-05, 2018')

question: How do top LLM-based bug-fixing agent systems differ in which SWE-bench Verified issues they solve, in fault localization, and in the value of bug reproduction?
hypothesis: Cases solved by all systems have higher-quality issue descriptions than cases solved by none; related reproduction scripts are more likely when the issue has better reproduction info.
contributions: First study of the effectiveness of LLM-based agents in automatic bug fixing for code repositories
Examines fault localization effectiveness across agents and their differences
Investigates the impact of bug reproduction on bug fixing
Summarizes current issues and future research directions

method.summary: Post-hoc analysis of the submitted patches and trajectories of six leaderboard systems on SWE-bench Verified: overlap of solved cases, issue-quality scoring with DeepSeek-R1, file and symbol-level fault localization from final patches, and a purpose-built two-agent system (RepoFixer, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) whose reproduction scripts are run before and after the golden patch.
method.task: Automated bug fixing on SWE-bench Verified (repository-level issue resolution)

datasets.name: SWE-bench Verified
datasets.source: Human-annotated subset of SWE-bench (2,294 instances, 12 Python repos), from OpenAI with SWE-bench authors
datasets.preprocessing: Golden-patch files and symbols extracted via AST; delta used to make show-line golden patch for line-level scoring

models.name: W&B Programmer
models.architecture: OpenAI o1 high-reasoning, GPT-4o memory compression, 5 parallel rollouts with o1 crosscheck tie-breaker

models.name: Blackbox AI Agent
models.architecture: ReAct with repo tools and bash

models.name: CodeStory Midwit Agent
models.architecture: Monte Carlo Tree Search, trajectory filtering by mean step reward

models.name: Learn-by-interact
models.architecture: Offline-collected interaction trajectories used as in-context examples

models.name: Devlo
models.architecture: Tools incl. reproduction_test and edge_case_test to filter candidate patches

models.name: Emergent E1
models.architecture: Multiple expert agents, then select final patch from candidates

models.name: RepoFixer (Searcher + Fixer)
models.architecture: Two-agent ReAct-like; Searcher returns suspicious code symbols; Fixer writes reproduction script, runs it, patches, re-runs

other.tools: Claude official bash and str_replace_editor; standard Function Call interface

other.use: scores issue quality on five metrics; five annotations per metric per instance, majority option kept

inference.samples: Six leaderboard systems: one submission each as submitted, no reruns. RepoFixer: one run per instance (500 reproduction scripts). DeepSeek-R1 judge: 5 annotations per metric per instance, majority vote.
inference.prompting: RepoFixer system prompt tells Fixer to write reproduction script, run it, self-assess reproduction, then patch and re-run script until resolved or turn limit. Full issue-quality prompts only on the authors' homepage.

parameters.reproduction_check: script run before and after golden patch in separate Docker instances; status change = 'related reproduction script'

metrics.name: Resolved cases
metrics.definition: count of the 500 instances whose submitted patch passes the Fail-to-Pass tests

metrics.name: File/symbol-level FL hit
metrics.definition: cases where at least one (or all) golden-patch files or code symbols appear in files/symbols modified by the final submitted patch

metrics.name: Related reproduction script rate
metrics.definition: share of reproduction scripts whose output status differs before vs after golden patch

baselines: The six systems compared against each other
eval.protocol: Single submitted result per system; manual trajectory inspection of 5 + 5 extreme cases plus 10 more by two authors who reconciled by discussion; DeepSeek-R1 judge cross-checked against regex rules on 500 issues (34 disagreements); no significance test on resolve rates.

availability.data: same repository (experimental data and issue quality annotation prompts)

limits: Differences in LLM backbone across closed-source systems are uncontrolled; no ablation with identical backbones
One submitted run per system; stochasticity not measured, assumes leaderboard results are best performance
Pass/fail via Fail-to-Pass tests only, which may be incomplete; patch correctness may be overstated
Reproduction-script quality is judged by output divergence before/after golden patch, which can misclassify scripts that do not trigger the bug
Issue quality is scored by DeepSeek-R1, checked against humans only on a subset; only 34 disagreements against regex checked
Python-only repos; manual analysis limited to 5 + 5 + 10 cases
No experiment isolates the effect of reproduction or patch verification on resolve rate: the reproduction claim is correlational with issue quality, and RepoFixer has no ablation
FL derived from final patches, not intermediate FL results
Leaderboard systems and models (o1, Claude 3.5 Sonnet Oct 2024) are late-2024 era and have dated
